To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lectins recognize carbohydrate ligands with a certain degree of flexibility, which may even include a selection of conformers by the binding site of the lectin.
lectin ligands are not rigid, and that the dynamic behavior of lectin ligands is not random, but rather is controlled by the lectins.
lectin ligands are dynamic entities, and that lectins can select the most suitable conformer for binding.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the elucidation of the structural and dynamical features of carbohydrate ligands, the elucidation of carbohydrate-lectin interactions and the development of a novel approach to rational marker/drug discovery.
the following questions: (i) What is the structure of a carbohydrate ligand?
the following topics: (a) lectin-ligand interactions, (b) carbohydrate modeling and (c) carbohydrate-based marker/drug design.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the recognition process between lectin and carbohydrate is a dynamic process in which the ligand is the active component.
the sugar code can be decoded only if the dynamic behavior of both the lectin and its ligand is taken into account.
the recognition of a carbohydrate ligand is a dynamic process, which may be influenced by the lectin and the ligand.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of X-ray crystallographic, nuclear magnetic resonance and computational studies has provided a deeper understanding of carbohydrate recognition by lectins.
we have been able to show that lectins do select a specific conformer from a mixture of conformers.
the recognition of a lectin by its ligand is a dynamic process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conformational flexibility of oligosaccharide ligands must not be underestimated in lectin binding studies.

the recognition of carbohydrate ligands by proteins is not a static process but a dynamic one, which can be described in terms of the interplay between a lectin and its ligand(s) as an interplay between a rigid and a flexible partner.
a carbohydrate ligand can move rather freely between several low-energy positions, and that this is the basis for conformers selection by a lectins.
